description: baseline linalg/qr_v2
Replace torch.geqrf with a CUTE DSL batched Householder QR path specialized for n=512 high-batch cases, using one CTA group per matrix panel and preserving FP32 compact H/tau outputs.
CUTE rankdef probe failed validation because tensor indexing produced a Float32 scalar without load()
CUTE rankdef probe still failed validation because ReductionOp is not exposed in installed CUTE DSL
CUTE rankdef probe still failed validation because tensor scalar indexing did not expose an atomic pointer
Added a CUTE DSL 512x512 tail-zero probe and rank-deficient shortcut that factors the leading 384 columns, improving the rankdef benchmark while falling back to torch.geqrf elsewhere
Added a second n=512 clustered-matrix shortcut that factors the leading 256 columns when the trailing half is tiny, improving the clustered benchmark and overall geomean

Best metric 109309.250 us at daf1d286af2c44ad29044d7d17e528eb0e22c34c versus 117381.362 us baseline (~6.9% faster). Working path uses CUTE DSL to probe exact 512 rank-deficient tails and routes rankdef to a 384-column geqrf, plus a clustered 512 shortcut that routes tiny trailing halves to a 256-column geqrf; both passed full validation and guards. Failed attempts were CUTE API issues around scalar load/reduction/atomic pointer use; next brief should pursue a true panel Householder kernel rather than more shape heuristics, or replace the torch reductions in the clustered detector with a CUTE probe to reduce overhead.
Optimize the best n=512 shortcut branch by replacing expensive torch tail detectors with cheaper CUTE DSL probes or fused reductions, preserving rankdef and clustered routing correctness.
Replaced torch clustered detector with a CUTE per-matrix paired-column probe; correctness passed but benchmark regressed from parent because the stricter detector missed clustered routing
Relaxed the CUTE clustered detector to an absolute tail threshold so clustered routing is restored; validation passed and benchmark matched parent within noise but did not improve
Changed both CUTE detectors to a scalar flag to avoid per-matrix flag allocation/reduction; validation passed but benchmark remained slightly slower than parent
Added a sparse CUTE clustered-tail sampler over four tail columns per row, replacing torch amax detector while preserving clustered routing; validation passed and benchmark improved versus parent

Best brief-1 metric was 109272.061 us at b0136cec65274efa6674af399a4bd469f74f272a, a small improvement over parent 109309.250 us. The winning change replaced the expensive torch clustered amax detector with a sparse CUTE DSL tail sampler over four tail columns per row; full paired-column CUTE and scalar-flag variants were correct but slower. Final nsys profile is captured for the winning commit. Next brief could tune the sparse sample pattern/threshold or fuse both rankdef and clustered probes into one CUTE launch.
Combine the best sparse CUTE 512 clustered detector with worker 1's 1024-plus rectangular shortcut experiments, keeping only improvements that preserve the 109272-us baseline branch correctness.
Combined worker 1 large rank-deficient CUTE probes and 3/4-column geqrf shortcut with the sparse 512 clustered detector; validation passed and benchmark improved slightly versus the parent.

Removed the 2048 large-rankdef probe while keeping worker 1's 1024 CUTE rank-deficient mask and 3/4-column shortcut alongside the sparse 512 clustered detector; validation passed and benchmark improved again.

Tested a lighter 1024 rank-deficient path that skips worker 1's mixed-batch split and only shortcuts all-rankdef batches; validation passed but benchmark regressed, so the mixed split is worth keeping.
Restored the mixed 1024 rank-deficient split after the all-rankdef-only variant regressed; validation passed and final benchmark returned to the combined design within noise.

Brief exhausted. Best metric was 109235.196 us at 79a1056a33cdc625edc2bbbc64664496d9d57228, combining worker 0's sparse CUTE 512 clustered detector with worker 1's 1024 CUTE rank-deficient mask and mixed-batch 3/4-column shortcut, while dropping the 2048 probe. Full combined 1024+2048 was correct but only reached 109245.051 us, and removing the mixed split regressed to 109317.913 us, so the best keep-set is 1024 mixed rankdef plus existing 512 CUTE shortcuts. Final HEAD restores that best design and has a fresh nsys profile; next brief should either tune the 1024 probe/split overhead or pursue a true CUTE Householder panel kernel rather than more detector pruning.
Explore batch-aware CUTE DSL routing on the current best branch: specialize benchmark batch sizes to avoid unnecessary probes and try separate fast paths for homogeneous versus mixed 512 batches.

Added batch-aware n=512 routing that uses CUTE DSL rankdef and clustered probes to split mixed 640-matrix batches into dense full-geqrf, rankdef 384-column, and clustered 256-column paths; validation passed and benchmark improved versus parent.

Specialized the batch-aware n=512 router so homogeneous rankdef and clustered 640-matrix batches reuse the already-computed CUTE probe flags instead of re-entering helper probe paths; validation passed and benchmark improved slightly.

Tested a batch=640 n=512 scalar sentinel to skip CUTE probes on dense-looking batches; validation passed but benchmark regressed badly because clustered/rankdef homogeneous cases were misrouted by the sentinel, so this path is discarded.

Brief exhausted. Best metric was 108896.632 us at 2dd4e7b7435a8e3dd055aab99cf85a919bc116df, improving over parent 2652fb77's 109220.646 us by using batch-aware n=512 CUTE routing. The winning path reuses CUTE rankdef flags to split 640-matrix batches into dense full geqrf plus rankdef 384-column and clustered 256-column sub-batches, then inlines homogeneous rankdef/clustered assembly to avoid redundant probe helper calls. A scalar dense sentinel validated but regressed to 114954.066 us by misrouting homogeneous clustered/rankdef cases, so it was logged and discarded. Final nsys profile is saved as profiles/2026-06-24-03-43-38-qrv2_kernel_languages_ohzemi9pv/worker-0-brief-3-iteration-1-2dd4e7b7435a8e3dd055aab99cf85a919bc116df.nsys-rep; next useful brief should move beyond routing heuristics toward a true CUTE Householder/panel QR replacement or CUTE output scatter to reduce boolean-index overhead.
Explore CUTE DSL or torch-light fast paths for small n=32/176/352 benchmark shapes on the current best branch, targeting reduced launch and geqrf overhead without harming large-shape routing.
Early-return n<512 shapes directly to geqrf to avoid large-shape structural probes.
Cached torch.ops.aten.geqrf dispatch validated but did not improve over direct torch.geqrf.
Explicit n==32/176/352 routing validated but was slower than generic n<512 early return.

Brief exhausted. Best committed candidate was 4b2cb360 with metric 108854.084635 us, improving parent 108896.632 by early-returning n<512 directly to torch.geqrf before large-shape CUTE probes. Cached ATen geqrf dispatch (108861.627673) and explicit n==32/176/352 routing (108857.402818) validated but were slower, so they were reverted. Final HEAD f3e72295 preserves the best code plus revert history and has an nsys profile captured; further small dense QR speedups likely require a real compact-H small-n QR implementation rather than routing tweaks.
Attempt a real CUTE DSL compact-H QR implementation for the small n=32 benchmark shape first, returning exact FP32 Householder factors and falling back for n=176/352 if needed.

Added a real CUTE DSL n=32 compact Householder QR kernel with one serial thread per matrix; full validation passed but benchmark regressed because the serial CUTE implementation made the small shape about 497 us.

Replaced the serial n=32 CUTE QR with a one-warp-per-matrix Householder kernel using warp reductions for norms and reflector dots; validation passed and benchmark improved to 101495.776 us overall with the n=32 shape at about 124 us.
Packed four n=32 QR matrices per CUTE CTA using one warp each; validation passed but n=32 slowed to about 154 us and overall regressed to 103286.086 us versus the one-warp-per-CTA version.
Reverted the slower four-warps-per-CTA variant back to the best one-warp-per-matrix CUTE QR32 kernel; validation passed and benchmark measured 101493.329 us, the best result in this brief.

Removed the per-column inner warp sync inside the n=32 CUTE QR reflector update while keeping the inter-panel sync; validation passed and benchmark improved to 101366.198 us with n=32 at about 123.7 us.

Best metric 101366.198 us at 93b347ecc8673e0ddf581f68c7f484ca0440cf2d, versus parent 108846-ish us and baseline 117381.362 us. The winning path is a real CUTE DSL n=32 compact Householder QR: one warp per matrix, warp reductions for column norms and reflector dot products, with one unnecessary inner sync removed; it passed full validation and guards, and final nsys profile is captured. Failed/slower branches were a serial one-thread CUTE QR32 kernel (correct but ~497 us for n=32) and a four-warps-per-CTA packing attempt (correct but slower than one-warp-per-CTA). Next brief could either profile-driven tune the QR32 kernel further (less global-memory traffic / shared or register staging) or try analogous CUTE QR for n=176/352.
Micro-tune the winning one-warp n=32 CUTE QR kernel for memory traffic and register staging, keeping compact-H math identical and accepting only full-benchmark wins over 101366 us.
Register-staged n=32 CUTE QR kept compact-H correctness but made the full benchmark exceed the 210s wrapper timeout, likely from register pressure/code size.
Cached the active QR32 column value via warp shuffle and reused the Householder vector entry across trailing-column updates; validation passed and full benchmark improved to 97227.825 us.
Removing QR32 warp syncs still validated but made the full benchmark exceed the 210s timeout, so the synchronization barriers appear needed for codegen/performance stability.
